title: GTA 6 vs GTA 5: The 15 Biggest Differences (Side by Side)

sections.text: In 2013, GTA 5 gave us Los Santos. Tomorrow, GTA 6 drops us into Leonida. Thirteen years apart. And after going through everything Rockstar has shown and said, I can tell you this: it is not GTA 5 with better graphics. The cops remember what you look like. Your guns don't disappear into your pocket anymore. And the cash on you is no longer safe. So here are the fifteen biggest differences between GTA 5 and GTA 6, side by side. Quick note before we start: when something comes from Rockstar or from a hands-on preview, I'll tell you where it's from. Nothing in this video is made up.

sections.label: THE SETTING
sections.text: Number fifteen: the setting. GTA 5 was Los Santos, Rockstar's take on Los Angeles, plus the deserts and mountains of Blaine County. Sun, smog, Hollywood, and a lot of empty desert. GTA 6 goes back to Vice City for the first time since Vice City Stories in 2006. But Vice City is only one part of it. The whole game takes place in the state of Leonida, Rockstar's version of Florida. Neon beaches, swamps, tiny island towns, and plenty of very Florida-style chaos. Leonida is the stage. Vice City is just its biggest city.

sections.label: THE MAP
sections.text: Number fourteen: the map itself. GTA 5's world was basically two halves: the city in the south, and Blaine County up north. GTA 6 splits Leonida into six named regions. Vice City. The Leonida Keys. Grassrivers, which is clearly the Everglades. Port Gellhorn. Ambrosia. And Mount Kalaga National Park. Now here's the honest part: Rockstar has not given an official size. You'll see a lot of numbers online, but they're estimates. What we can see is a single state with a big city, islands, swamps, farmland and mountains, all in one map.

sections.label: WILDLIFE
sections.text: Number thirteen: the wildlife. GTA 5 had animals. Deer, cougars, sharks, and of course Chop. But they were mostly background. In GTA 6's trailers, nature is everywhere. Alligators walking through the wetlands, flamingos taking off over the water, and yes, a gator walking into a convenience store. In Grassrivers, the swamp doesn't look like scenery. It looks like a place you'll want to stay out of after dark.

sections.label: WEATHER
sections.text: Number twelve: the weather. In GTA 5, weather was a simple cycle. Sunny, cloudy, rain, the occasional thunderstorm. According to Edge's preview, GTA 6's clouds are shaped by wind, humidity, fog, time of day and even seasons. And Game Informer reports that tropical storms and hurricanes are in the game. Rockstar hasn't said how often a hurricane hits, or what it does to gameplay. But a GTA set in Florida, with hurricanes? That's going to create some wild moments.

sections.label: THINGS TO DO
sections.text: Number eleven: things to do outside the missions. GTA 5 had golf, tennis, yoga and triathlons. Most of us tried them once. GTA 6's previews list fan boats, basketball, scuba diving, kayaking, BASE jumping, skydiving, dirt biking and weightlifting, and that's just what's been shown so far. And these activities aren't on a menu. They're part of the world: a basketball court on the beach, a fan boat in the swamp, a gym down the street.

sections.label: YOUR BODY
sections.text: Number ten: your character's body. In GTA 5, Michael, Franklin and Trevor looked exactly the same from the first mission to the last. GTA 6 brings back something San Andreas fans have wanted for years. Previews report that the game tracks stats like health, cardio, stamina, strength, calories and body fat. You need a gym membership, and a daily workout takes three exercises. Whether your weight changes how the game plays, or only how you look, Rockstar hasn't fully explained yet.

sections.label: SOCIAL MEDIA
sections.text: Number nine: social media. GTA 5 made fun of Facebook with Lifeinvader, a website you could open on your phone. GTA 6 builds social media into the world itself. Both trailers are packed with vertical phone videos, livestreams and viral clips. And in the extended gameplay look, livestream chat popped up during a police chase. In Leonida, if you do something stupid in public, someone is probably filming it.

sections.label: THE PEOPLE
sections.text: Number eight: the people of Leonida. Here's a number from the previews: GTA 6's characters have around six hundred thousand animations. The same coverage puts GTA 5 at around fifty-five thousand. Rockstar also has a team writing ambient dialogue, and pedestrians have their own routines, jobs and reactions. So the crowd on the beach isn't just walking in circles. Every one of them is supposed to be doing something.

sections.label: THE HARDWARE
sections.text: Number seven: the hardware. GTA 5 launched in 2013 on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, and came to newer consoles and PC later. GTA 6 launches only on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. Rockstar has confirmed it targets thirty frames per second on all consoles at launch, with extras like ray-traced shadows on PS5 Pro. There's no PC version at launch. It's built for this generation only, and the lighting in the trailers shows it.

sections.label: SPECIAL ABILITIES
sections.text: Number six: special abilities. In GTA 5, every character had a superpower. Michael slowed down time in gunfights. Franklin slowed down time behind the wheel. And Trevor went into a rage and took less damage. In GTA 6, Jason and Lucia share one ability called Focus, a slow-motion aim that, according to Rockstar, works differently from Red Dead 2's Dead Eye. Three different powers became one shared one. And that says a lot about how this game treats the duo.

sections.label: STEALING CARS
sections.text: Number five: stealing cars. In GTA 5, grand theft auto was one button. Smash the window, drive away. In GTA 6, Edge reports that newer cars can have trackers that broadcast where they are, and owners can report the theft. Some drivers panic and run, some fight back, and for older cars you'll have tools like a slim jim. The most expensive car on the street is no longer the smartest one to take.

sections.label: MONEY
sections.text: Number four: money. In GTA 5, your money was just one number, and dying cost you a hospital bill. GTA 6 splits it up. Rockstar describes three ways to hold money: cash on you, an ATM card, and a digital balance in a bank app called BuckMe. Money in the bank is safe. Cash in your pocket isn't, previews report you can lose it when you die. And loot from robberies has to go through a fence before it's worth anything. So after a big job, your first stop isn't the strip club. It's the ATM.

sections.label: WEAPONS
sections.text: Number three: weapons. GTA 5 let you carry an entire army in your pockets. Rocket launchers, miniguns, ten rifles, all invisible. GTA 6 ends that. According to Rockstar's Rob Nelson, you can conceal two handguns and carry two long guns, but only one fits on your back, so the second one stays in your hands. Long guns are visible, people react to them, and your full loadout lives in your personal vehicle. Walk into a store with a shotgun on your back, and the store will notice.

sections.label: THE PROTAGONISTS
sections.text: Number two: the protagonists. GTA 5 had three men who barely trusted each other. Michael, the retired bank robber. Franklin, the hustler. And Trevor, well, Trevor. GTA 6 has two: Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, partners in crime and partners in life. Lucia is the first female lead of the modern GTA era. You can still switch between them like in GTA 5, and they can hold hands, open doors for each other and even work out together. GTA 5 was three stories that crossed. GTA 6 is one relationship under pressure.

sections.label: THE POLICE
sections.text: And number one: the police. In GTA 5, losing the cops was easy. Break their line of sight, hide in an alley, wait for the circles to disappear, and they forgot you ever existed. In GTA 6, that's over. Rob Nelson said a crime needs a witness or an alarm before it's even reported. But once the police have a description, they remember your car, your clothes and your appearance. To get clean, you have to deal with each one. Swap the car, change the outfit, lay low. The wanted level now goes up to six stars. And on top of that, a criminal profile tracks how you play over time, a bit like Red Dead 2's honor system. GTA 5's cops chased you. GTA 6's cops investigate you.

But honestly, the biggest difference between these two games isn't on this list. It's time. When GTA 5 came out, some of you weren't even born. Some of you played it in high school, and now you're going to play GTA 6 with a job and an alarm clock. Thirteen years of trailers, rumors and memes, and tomorrow it's finally real. So tell me in the comments: which of these differences are you most hyped for? And subscribe, because this channel is going all in on GTA 6, every single day, from launch day on. I'll see you in Leonida.
